questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) State any three (03) health concerns associated with prolonged use of the computer. (3 marks)

(ii) Briefly describe measures that can be taken to reduce or prevent each of the health concerns you identified in a(i) above. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Three health concerns (3 marks, 1 mark each)**

Any three of the following:

- **Eye strain** (computer vision syndrome): tired, dry or blurred eyes and headaches after staring at the screen for a long time.
- **Back and neck pain** caused by sitting for hours in a bad posture.
- **Repetitive strain injury (RSI)**, for example carpal tunnel syndrome, pain in the wrists, hands and fingers caused by repeated typing and mouse use.
- **Headaches, stress and fatigue.**
- **Obesity and poor circulation** caused by sitting for too long without moving.

**(ii) Measures to reduce or prevent each concern (3 marks, 1 mark each)**

| Health concern | Preventive measure |
|---|---|
| Eye strain | Rest the eyes regularly (look away from the screen for a few seconds every 20 minutes), adjust the brightness and contrast, use an anti-glare screen or filter, avoid glare and reflections from windows and lamps. |
| Back and neck pain | Use an adjustable chair with back support, keep the back straight, feet flat on the floor, and place the top of the screen at eye level. |
| RSI | Use a wrist rest and a keyboard and mouse placed at elbow height, keep the wrists straight, take short breaks and do hand and wrist exercises. |
| Headaches, stress, fatigue | Take regular breaks, work in a well-lit and well-ventilated room, avoid working for too long without stopping. |
| Obesity, poor circulation | Stand up and walk about every hour, do physical exercise. |

(b) Briefly explain what is meant by;

(i) Database normalization. (2 marks)

(ii) Data consistency. (2 marks)

(iii) Data redundancy. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Database normalization (2 marks).** Normalization is the process of organising the data of a database into well-designed tables, following a series of rules called normal forms (1NF, 2NF, 3NF), in order to remove unnecessary repetition of data and to avoid insertion, update and deletion errors. Large tables are split into smaller related tables that are linked by keys.

**(ii) Data consistency (2 marks).** Data consistency means that the same data is the same everywhere it is stored or used in the database: there are no contradictions. For example, a student's address must be identical in every table or copy where it appears, so that after an update no old value remains.

**(iii) Data redundancy (2 marks).** Data redundancy is the unnecessary repetition (duplication) of the same data in a database or file system, for example the same customer address stored in many records. It wastes storage space and can lead to inconsistency when only some of the copies are updated.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Briefly describe the following computing terminologies.

(i) Client-server network (2 marks)

(ii) Peer to peer network (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Client-server network (2 marks).** A network in which one or more powerful, dedicated computers, called servers, store data and provide services (file storage, printing, e-mail, security, Internet access) to the other computers, called clients, which send requests to the servers. The network is managed centrally, which makes security, backup and user control easier.

**(ii) Peer to peer network (2 marks).** A network in which all the computers have the same status (there is no dedicated server): each computer can share its own files, printers and other resources directly with the others and can also use theirs, so each one acts both as a client and as a server. It is cheap and simple, and suits small networks such as a small office or a home.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) What is a biometric system? (2 marks)

(ii) Describe any two examples of biometric data. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Biometric system (2 marks).** A biometric system is a security system that identifies or verifies a person from a unique physical or behavioural characteristic of that person. A sensor captures the characteristic, and the system compares it with the template stored in its database to grant or refuse access.

**(ii) Two examples of biometric data (2 marks, 1 mark each)**

Any two of the following:

- **Fingerprint:** the pattern of ridges and valleys on a finger, which is different for each person and is read by a fingerprint scanner.
- **Face:** the shape and position of facial features (eyes, nose, mouth), captured by a camera.
- **Iris or retina:** the unique pattern of the coloured part of the eye (iris) or of the blood vessels at the back of the eye (retina).
- **Voice:** the unique features of a person's voice (pitch, tone, rhythm) captured by a microphone.
- **Signature or hand geometry:** the shape and the way of writing a signature, or the size and shape of the hand.
